title: A Contact Is Not a Channel

scenes.tts: A cochlear implant can have up to 22 contacts. Yet in one study of 18 adult implant users, speech scores stopped improving at 8 to 10 channels. So what is a channel? And why does an electrode in the eye not make a pixel?
scenes.visual: A row of 22 contacts along the implant array; a bracket marks 8 to 10 with a question mark; then a retina with an electrode and a question-mark pixel.
scenes.narration: A cochlear implant can have up to 22 contacts. Yet in one study of 18 adult implant users, speech scores stopped improving at 8 to 10 channels. So what is a channel? And why does an electrode in the eye not make a pixel?

scenes.tts: A contact is hardware on the array, and a channel is a band of frequency information. Clinical maps give higher frequencies to basal contacts and lower ones to apical contacts. Neighbouring contacts make overlapping electric fields, called channel interaction. So many contacts do not give as many independent channels. The plateau depends on array type and placement.
scenes.visual: Array with base and apex ends labelled, high and low frequency; fields of neighbouring contacts overlap and the overlap is shaded; the count of channels drops below the count of contacts.

scenes.tts: An eye is a camera, so a grid of electrodes should make a grid of dots. But an electrode on the retina's inner surface sits over ganglion-cell axons running to the optic disk. Current excites these axons of passage, and the percept follows the places the axons serve. Four adults with Argus implants often drew elongated or distorted shapes from single electrodes, and an axon model accounted for them. That is a model-supported explanation, not a direct recording.
scenes.visual: Expected: one electrode, one dot. Then the retina schematic: axons run past the electrode toward the optic disk; the passing axons light up and the dot stretches into a streak labelled as model-supported.
scenes.narration: An eye is a camera, so a grid of electrodes should make a grid of dots. But an electrode on the retina's inner surface sits over ganglion-cell axons running to the optic disk. scenes.tts: The PRIMAvera study was open-label and single-arm, in adults with geographic atrophy. 38 people were implanted, 32 were assessed at twelve months, and 26 of those 32 met the endpoint. That is about 81 percent of those assessed. Count the six unassessed as not meeting it, and it is about 68 percent of those implanted.
scenes.visual: 38 person dots; 32 outlined as assessed; 26 filled as met the endpoint; two fractions with different denominators appear in turn.
scenes.narration: The PRIMAvera study was open-label and single-arm, in adults with geographic atrophy. 38 people were implanted, 32 were assessed at twelve months, and 26 of those 32 met the endpoint. That is about 81 percent of those assessed. Count the six unassessed as not meeting it, and it is about 68 percent of those implanted.

scenes.tts: The endpoint was a gain of at least 0.2 log MAR, measured with the PRIMA glasses. There, participants could adjust zoom from 1 to 12 times, so a zoomed score measures the implant plus a magnifier. Without zoom or image processing, mean implant resolution was 1.32 log MAR. Twenty times ten to the power of 1.32 is about 417, so 20 over 417. Native resolution and zoom-assisted reading are separate measurements.

scenes.tts: Serious events belong beside the benefit: 19 participants had 26 serious device- or procedure-related events. So ask what was counted. Contacts are not channels, electrodes are not pixels, and people assessed are not people implanted. Native resolution is not zoomed reading.
scenes.visual: The safety count, then four pairs, each with a not-equal sign: contacts and channels, electrodes and pixels, assessed and implanted, native and zoomed; the safety count sits beside.
